leads_not_followed.what: ANSWERED DURING THIS SURVEY, recorded here as the headline result: the Samsung EM32DX is locally driveable over MDC on TCP 1515 with no cloud and no app. What remains open is the exact byte-level content mechanism and its durability
leads_not_followed.why_promising: I opened this as the survey's biggest unknown and closed it. Two independent repos confirm the capability (vgavro/samsung-mdc, 109 stars, explicitly listing EM32DX; WeeJeWel/node-samsung-emdx, a one-line show-image CLI stated to work without cloud or app). What I did NOT verify first-hand is the mechanism detail reported from the upstream issue threads — a content.json whose image_url points at the user's own local HTTP server, a sub-256-byte URL limit, and a requirement that the content UUID change on every update or the panel will not refresh. Worth reading vgavro/samsung-mdc issues #20, #21, #22 and #24 before writing code, and worth checking whether Samsung firmware updates preserve the behaviour, since Samsung does not document it.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether the reverse-engineered Visionect PV3 device protocol server (timeframe/ha-addon) can be extended from the 13in Place & Play to the 32in — which would remove the licence kill switch entirely
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This is the one lead that could rescue Visionect. Its REST API is the best-documented integration in the survey, but a self-hosted VSS stops working without a valid VSS_LICENSE_ID, which is a remote kill switch held by a 47-person company. timeframe/ha-addon already contains a clean-room TCP server implementing the device wire protocol on port 11114, with a documented 20-byte header, a 4bpp/16-level greyscale LZ4 strip encoder, and even an MITM proxy used to derive it — but it is written for 1600x1200 13in panels. Extending the encoder to the 32in's 2560x1440 would give licence-free operation on hardware he owns. Non-trivial but bounded, and the hard protocol work is already done and published.

leads_not_followed.what: LARGELY ANSWERED: ADB works on the Tableaux platform. What remains is confirming APK install (not just file push) on the 25.3in and 32in specifically, and whether network ADB works or a USB cable is always required
leads_not_followed.why_promising: A hobbyist has verifiably pushed image files onto a Tableaux over `adb push` into /storage/emulated/0/Pictures/ and driven it with scrcpy, and four commercial CMS vendors integrate by sideloading their own APK — so the platform is open. Two gaps remain. First, `adb install` on the 25.3in/32in is reported from a CMS vendor's certified-device guide that I did not fetch myself. Second, NO source shows network ADB (adb connect <ip>:5555) on any Philips signage display; every example uses USB, so provisioning may need physical access — fine for one-time setup, awkward if he wants remote recovery. Also worth an empirical test: whether SICP responds on TCP 5000 (`nc <ip> 5000`), since the SICP spec lists no ePaper model and neither Tableaux manual mentions it — though SICP is control-only and would not carry images anyway.

leads_not_followed.what: The resolution and PPI of the E Ink 25.3in Spectra 6 module (ED2208-PEA, in stock at $1,400), AND whether any TCON or controller exists that a non-specialist could use to drive a Mini-LVDS 25.3in panel
leads_not_followed.why_promising: No finished product pairs Spectra 6 colour with a 25.3in high-PPI panel — the shipping Spectra 6 devices are all 93 PPI 31.5in units, while the 145 PPI 25.3in devices are all lower-quality Kaleido or older ACeP. If this module is 3200x1800 it would be the best fine-art e-paper surface in existence. TWO THINGS TO CORRECT FROM MY FIRST PASS, both of which make this harder than it looked: the E Ink listing does not publish resolution at all, and 25.3in panels use Mini-LVDS requiring a TCON or FPGA, so the Modos Glider pairing I initially suggested is not viable (Glider tops out around 224 MP/s versus the 364 MP/s a 25.3in 3200x1800 needs at 60Hz). Ask E Ink for both the datasheet AND what its 'Vision Driving Board' actually supports — that board is the only named controller path and I could not find any documentation for it.

leads_not_followed.what: CORRECTION WORTH PROPAGATING: the widely-repeated claim that Modos Glider drives 4in-42in e-paper panels is false, and there is currently NO open-source controller for any panel over 15 inches
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Recorded as a lead because the error is in press coverage and will keep resurfacing. The '4 to 42 inch' range comes from an appendix Screen List in Glider's README that carries an explicit disclaimer — 'This is a list of all E-ink screens that have public information available, not a list of screens that's compatible with the Glider' — and the largest panel marked Tested there is 5.0in, with the compatibility table topping out at 13.3in. The bandwidth ceilings confirm it. Separately, epdiy (1.9k stars) supports nothing above 13.3in, ESPHome's waveshare_epaper caps at 13.3in mono / 7.3in colour, and Inkplate's largest is 13.3in. The practical consequence: the ONLY >15in self-build route today is the QSPI 31.5in Spectra 6 panel with Good Display's own ESP32-S3 kit. If he wants a bare-panel build, that is the one to buy.

leads_not_followed.what: ANSWERED AND IT IS BAD NEWS: a lapsed Visionect licence stops the devices working even on a self-hosted server. What remains open is the current price and whether any perpetual option exists
leads_not_followed.why_promising: I opened this as the question standing between Visionect's excellent API and a clean recommendation, and the answer disqualifies it for most purposes. Visionect's installation docs state 'The VSS_LICENSE_ID environmental variable must be set in order for the VSS to function. Without a proper value for the license, the devices will not be able to operate.' A developer who deployed them reports the on-premise fee arrived around 2021 at $7/month per device after years of being free. visionect.com/pricing returns HTTP 404, so the current figure is unknown — ask Visionect directly for the Essential plan price, the term, and whether a perpetual licence exists, and note that a shareholder (STH Ventures) is in liquidation.

leads_not_followed.what: Samsung Color E-Paper 25-inch (3200x1800) — is it actually purchasable anywhere?
leads_not_followed.why_promising: SIGNIFICANT and I could not close it. Samsung's ISE 2025 announcement listed a 25in at 3200x1800 alongside the 13in, 32in and 75in — that is Spectra-class colour at 145 PPI, the combination that would make Samsung both the safest vendor AND the best art panel. But it is absent from the US and Hong Kong storefronts I fetched, and samsung.com/us/business/smart-signage/e-paper/ returned a page with no e-paper SKUs listed at all. My WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted before I could sweep for regional listings. If a 25in EMDX exists to buy, it changes the shortlist.

leads_not_followed.what: Bigme B251 (non-Pro) 25.3in all-in-one monitor-and-PC with an onboard operating system
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Bigme sells a 25.3in colour e-ink device that is a complete computer rather than a monitor. If its onboard OS is Android or Linux and permits installing software, it would be a single-box solution — his renderer running on the display itself, no attached host, no cloud. I did not fetch the product page for this variant, so I have no verified specs, OS or price.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink's own 75-inch Spectra 6 colour ePaper display, and Samsung's 75in 5K EMDX
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both are outside my 'purchasable today' slice but bear on the 3-year view. E Ink's news index references a 75in Spectra 6 launch, and Samsung demonstrated a 75in 5K (5120x2880) at ISE 2025 with no announced price or availability. Meanwhile E Ink's H5 production line is now in volume production specifically for 32in and 55in panels, and H6 comes online in 2026 — so large colour panels are the direction of the whole industry, not a niche. A 55in colour panel would likely appear in products within his 3-year window.

leads_not_followed.what: RESOLVED: miractl is real and explicitly supports the Mira Pro 25.3in. No longer a gap
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Recorded only to close it out. The sourcehut URL returned HTTP 502 but github.com/elithper/miractl is live and confirms testing on both the Mira 13.3 and Mira Pro 25.3, controlling refresh mode, speed 1-7, contrast 0-15, dither mode, white/black filters, cool/warm front light and antiflicker, with five presets. Together with mira-js (63 stars), clarkema/miractl (Rust), rynom99/mira-cli and the 854-star timeframe/ha-addon, the BOOX Mira Pro has more independent working tooling than any other device in this survey.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink kit-store large panels not individually priced: 28in monochrome, 31.2in colour, 31.2in monochrome, 42in monochrome, and 25.3in Kaleido 3
leads_not_followed.why_promising: All appear in E Ink's own developer store inventory alongside the priced 25.3in modules, and the 42in monochrome panel is the largest e-paper surface available to a self-builder anywhere in this survey. Prices and resolutions were not shown on the listing pages I reached; a direct enquiry would open up the large-format self-build option considerably. Note Modos Glider is documented as driving panels up to 42in, so the pairing exists.

leads_not_followed.what: Soofa and MpicoSys — large-format e-paper signage vendors named in the brief's sweep list
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both were in scope for the commercial/signage category and I reached neither: my WebSearch budget was exhausted at 200 calls first. Soofa in particular sells large solar e-paper community signs. Based on the Papercast and Visionect pattern, expect municipal/B2B sales with a mandatory vendor cloud, but the possibility of a documented API makes them worth a check.

leads_not_followed.what: Independent measurement of Spectra 6 colour accuracy for reproductions — gamut volume, Delta-E, reflectance, bit depth, and whether any vendor publishes an ICC profile
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This is a hole across EVERY device in the survey and it matters specifically for fine art. Not one vendor publishes a colour profile, a gamut volume, a Delta-E figure or a documented dithering approach; E Ink's own Spectra 6 page publishes contrast (30:1) and PPI but no colour metrics at all. Colour-count claims for the very same 31.5in Spectra 6 panel range from 54,600 to 60,000 to 65,000 to 77,000 depending on whose marketing you read. Worse, Samsung and others apply an undocumented device-side 'colour imaging algorithm' to whatever image they receive. For controlled reproduction he needs either measured data or a device where he owns the dithering — which is the strongest single argument for the bare-panel-plus-Glider path.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Dalian Good Display has any formal standing with E Ink, and who E Ink's authorised Chinese module partners actually are
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Good Display is the practical source for large bare panels and matching controllers, so its film supply matters. I confirmed directly that E Ink's own partner listing does not name Good Display (it names PPDS/Philips, Sharp, AUO Display Plus, MediaTek and others), which suggests Good Display buys on ordinary commercial terms rather than as a partner. A subagent also reports that E Ink's named Chinese partner for flexible/OTFT displays is DKE, and that Good Display operates across at least eight domains with two legal entities sharing one ICP filing — both unverified by me. Worth resolving before designing a product around Good Display part numbers.

leads_not_followed.what: Geniatech direct sales enquiry - request the EPC2530 (25.3", 163 PPI, Android 11) SDK documentation, confirm whether the bundled CMS can be bypassed or self-hosted, whether APK sideloading is permitted, and what MOQ and unit price apply to a single unit
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This is the highest-value unresolved question in the whole slice. Geniatech is the only vendor combining credible corporate durability (27 years, own factory, diversified product lines) with an Android 11 applications processor, an in-house TCON, an explicitly advertised 'Open API & SDK', and the best-resolution large panel available (25.3" at 3200x1800). If the SDK is real and APKs can be sideloaded, this likely beats every consumer frame on both of the client's criteria simultaneously. None of it is published, so it can only be resolved by contacting them.

leads_not_followed.what: BLOOMIN8 local REST API - obtain or reverse-document the full API specification beyond what the Home Assistant component reveals, and confirm image resolution, colour space and dithering requirements for the 28.5" (2160x3060) model
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The BLOOMIN8 28.5" is the best size-plus-openness combination found. Its local HTTP API is real and mDNS-discoverable, but the contract is documented only by vendor-published Home Assistant code plus third-party libraries, not by a specification. For a client pushing gigapixel-derived renders, the exact expected input format and whether upload_dithered_image_data lets him supply his own dithering (rather than accepting the device's) is decisive for colour fidelity. The community CLI mrud/bloomin8-cli explicitly implements Spectra 6 dithering, so the answer is probably recoverable from that code.

leads_not_followed.what: Modos Flow 'Hacking Guide' campaign update (Jul 01, 2026) and the remaining Crowd Supply update series
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Modos published an update titled 'Hacking Guide' on 2026-07-01 plus 'Comparing the Paper Dev Kit with Flow' on 2026-06-18. These are the most likely place to find an authoritative statement on whether the Caster/Glider stack can be brought up on a large Spectra 6 panel and what waveform work that requires - the single biggest open technical question in the open-hardware route. Not read in this session.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Caster/Glider can render correct COLOUR on a Spectra 6 panel, as opposed to merely driving its LVDS timing
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Glider's documentation states support for panels up to 25.3" and handles the LVDS signalling those panels use, but Caster's stated panel scope is monochrome and colour-filter-array screens. Spectra 6 is a four-pigment microcup system, not a CFA, and needs its own multi-pass waveform set. The open-hardware route to a >15in COLOUR frame hinges entirely on this question and it is currently unresolved - worth raising directly on the Modos Discord/Matrix or in the Caster issue tracker before committing to that path.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink 'Vision' evaluation kit and Vision Driving Board specifications, plus the rest of E Ink's own driving-board family (HULK, THOR, ICE, Salt, Luvia, CONCERTO, Venus, Scarlet, RedHulk)
leads_not_followed.why_promising: E Ink sells the 31.5" Spectra 6 module directly through its own kit store and names the Vision Driving Board as the companion controller, but publishes neither per-board panel compatibility nor prices on the category listing. This is the manufacturer-sanctioned bare-panel-plus-controller route and is likely the lowest-risk self-build path for correct Spectra 6 colour, since the waveforms come from the panel maker. Individual board product pages were not reached in this session.

leads_not_followed.what: Good Display GDES285E01 (28.5" A2, 2160x3060) full datasheet and its interface type, plus whether a development kit exists for it
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This panel has arguably the best geometry-and-density combination above 15 inches for framed single works (A2 portrait, ~131 PPI), and it is the substrate under both the BLOOMIN8 28.5" and InkPoster Tela 28.5". But Good Display's product page is an unpopulated stub with no interface, dimensions, refresh or price, so a self-build at this size is currently undocumented. The downloadable spec sheet and a direct enquiry to info@good-display.com would settle it.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether the Philips Tableaux 5150I accepts a sideloaded Android APK, and whether PPDS publishes any API or SDK for its Android SoC platform
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Tableaux is the best durability-plus-plausible-programmability combination among established vendors: Android SoC, 16 GB storage, five local content paths, PoE, and explicit support for third-party management software rather than vendor-cloud-only. If APK sideloading is permitted, the client's own app could run on the display itself. The announcement does not state it either way, and no PPDS developer documentation was located.

leads_not_followed.what: Aura Ink - Aura Frames' entry into Spectra 6 colour ePaper frames, announced around 2025-10-21
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Aura Frames is an established, well-funded consumer digital-frame company with real retail distribution - a materially different staying-power profile from the crowdfunding entrants. Their move into Spectra 6 is exactly the kind of new entrant the client asked to have discovered. Not confirmed whether any Aura Ink model exceeds 15 inches, which is the gating question. Press-release URL was seen in search results but not fetched, so no URL is asserted here.

leads_not_followed.what: Reflection Frame and Inkjoy Frame - two further Spectra 6 crowdfunding photo/art frames
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both surfaced as additional crowdfunded Spectra 6 frames, evidencing how crowded this space has become. Sizes were not established and both are likely at or below 13.3 inches, which would place them out of scope - but they should be size-checked before being dismissed, and their pricing is relevant context for the category. URLs seen in search results only, not fetched.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink Marquee panel sizes, resolution and availability timing
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Marquee is E Ink's newest large-area colour platform, introduced at InfoComm 2026 and a Best in Show winner, with a -20 to 65 C range aimed at outdoor DOOH. E Ink has published essentially no specifications. If Marquee brings higher PPI or better colour at large sizes than Spectra 6, it changes the medium-term picture for this client - worth monitoring, though outdoor DOOH positioning suggests coarse pitch.

leads_not_followed.what: Samsung Color E-Paper 75" EMDX availability, price, and whether the Color E-Paper line exposes any API or accepts third-party applications (Tizen/MagicINFO/VXT)
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Samsung is the highest-durability entrant in the category and the loudest signal that large-format colour e-paper has gone mainstream. The 75" was showcased at ISE 2025 with no availability date. More useful for this client would be establishing whether the shipping 32" EM32DX can be driven by anything other than Samsung's own mobile app - if MagicINFO or a local HTTP path exists, a durable vendor becomes viable. Samsung newsroom pages timed out repeatedly in this session.

leads_not_followed.what: The claim that mass production of the world's first 30-inch-plus colour e-paper display has begun
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This article title indicates a mass-production milestone for a 30"+ colour e-paper panel, which would firm up the supply picture for the 31.5" module and identify the manufacturer doing volume production. The page was reachable but returned only navigation and membership chrome rather than article body in this session, so the company, date and panel details could not be extracted.

leads_not_followed.what: Melford Technologies datasheets for the 25.3", 28", 32" and 75" units, and identification of the underlying manufacturer
leads_not_followed.why_promising: A UK/EU procurement and warranty channel for the same panel ladder sold from China would materially reduce import, lead-time and support friction for a European buyer. The datasheets are offered for download and would also reveal which ODM sits behind these units - useful for cross-checking the chassis-sharing pattern already observed between Good Display and SEEKINK.

leads_not_followed.what: ePaint / Anhui Yutu ChLCD - obtain resolution, PPI, reflectance and measured colour data, and a physical sample
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The only >15in colour reflective displays found that are NOT built on E Ink panels, at 28", 31.5" and 55", with claimed sub-1-second refresh and up to 16 million colours - and the vendor itself names art galleries as a target market. If the resolution and reflectance are respectable this would break the E Ink single-supply dependency entirely. But no resolution figure is published anywhere on the site, and ChLCD is characteristically desaturated, so this needs measured data before it can be taken seriously.

leads_not_followed.what: Agile (E Ink ecosystem partner) - the 75" Kaleido 3 display and the 'Agile Conversion Engine' middleware
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Agile built a 75" Kaleido 3 display with E Ink and supplies conversion middleware. Kaleido 3 at large size is a different colour technology from Spectra 6 (colour-filter-array over monochrome, faster refresh, lower saturation, higher effective mono resolution), and a middleware layer implies a documented content pipeline. Worth investigating as an alternative colour approach and as a possible source of image-conversion tooling. Named on E Ink's InfoComm page but Agile's own site was not reached.

leads_not_followed.what: Fraimic's local-only mode protocol, and the backers-only campaign updates
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Fraimic advertises the strongest local-only claim of any consumer frame ('no third-party servers', 'No apps | No subscriptions') yet also requires an account at app.fraimic.com, and publishes no protocol. Most substantive updates (#10-#13, #15) are backers-only, so delivery quality and the local-mode mechanics are unverifiable from outside. If the local mode turns out to be a documented HTTP endpoint rather than a manual browser upload, the 31.5" Large Canvas at USD 1,299 becomes a much stronger candidate than currently rated.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Visionect has any colour (Spectra 6 or Kaleido) product on its roadmap
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Visionect's self-hosted RESTful JSON API with programmatic control of dithering method and bit-depth encoding is precisely the architecture this client needs, and its Place & Play 32" is in stock at EUR 2,300 - but it is monochrome, which disqualifies it for colour art. A colour Visionect model would immediately become the leading candidate in this entire survey. Worth a direct enquiry.

leads_not_followed.what: Independent measurement of Spectra 6 colour accuracy, gamut and ghosting at large sizes for art reproduction
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The single biggest evidence gap across every device in this slice. Not one vendor documents a colour profile, none publishes measured gamut, and no vendor or reviewer publishes ghosting characterisation for the large panels. All that exists are platform-level marketing figures (4,096 colours, ~85% NTSC, ~30:1 contrast, <=15s full refresh). For an archive of gigapixel scans where reproduction fidelity is the whole point, this needs resolving empirically - most likely by buying one panel or frame and measuring it, since the published record will not answer it.

leads_not_followed.what: Seeed Studio XIAO ePaper DIY Kit EE02 and Soldered Inkplate 13Spectra - 13.3" Spectra 6 open dev boards
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both are below the 15in floor so they are out of scope as targets, but both are ESP32-S3 open development boards for Spectra 6 colour panels with published toolchains. They are the cheapest way to prototype and validate the client's rendering, dithering and colour-conversion pipeline against real Spectra 6 hardware before committing to an expensive large panel - a genuinely useful de-risking step. URLs seen in search results only, not fetched.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether ANY 2025-2026 crowdfunded frame has actually delivered a unit larger than 15 inches to a backer
leads_not_followed.why_promising: THE HIGHEST-VALUE UNANSWERED QUESTION IN THIS SLICE. Several vendors advertise 25.3in, 28.5in and 31.5in. I found a documented slipped ship date (Fraimic, unconfirmed fulfilment as of 2026-07-27), a dormant storefront seven months post-campaign (InkJoy), and a product absent from its creator's own catalogue (BLOOMIN8) — but NO positive confirmation of large-format delivery from any of them. If none has shipped at size, the entire crowdfunding tier should be excluded from the development-target decision regardless of price. Requires a real browser session against Kickstarter comment threads.

leads_not_followed.what: PocketBook International's current revenue and headcount
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The Swiss entity files no accounts and holds only CHF 100,000 of capital with a single administrator. Aggregator snippets suggest a fall from US$151m (2010) to about US$11.1m (2025) and from 230 to about 120 staff. If true this materially undercuts the medium rating on the group that owns InkPoster AND IONNYK AND co-owns Bigme — i.e. the largest single concentration of credible options in this survey. All such pages (ZoomInfo, RocketReach, LeadIQ, D&B) are gated.

leads_not_followed.what: Kickstarter and BackerKit campaign pages for InkJoy, BLOOMIN8, MelonFrame, Memoir and Modos Flow
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Money raised, backer counts, and — critically — the comment threads and creator updates that reveal whether units shipped. Both sites return HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so this needs a real browser.

leads_not_followed.what: reMarkable's audited Annual Reports 2023 and 2024 and interim reports through Q1 2025
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Linked from remarkable.com/investor-relations and not opened. These are the only audited financials available for ANY vendor in this survey — revenue, EBITDA, cash position, debt covenants and going-concern language — and they bear directly on refinancing the NOK 500m bond maturing 2027-10-12. Even though reMarkable is out of scope on size, the reports are the best available calibration for what a 'healthy' vendor in this sector actually looks like.

leads_not_followed.what: Papercast's FY2024 full accounts (filed 2025-10-14) and the Christopher Bake charge instrument (MR01, delivered 2025-10-27)
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Together these would show whether the October 2025 event — both founders' PSC stakes extinguished, pre-emption rights removed, a personal charge granted to an incoming director — was growth capital or a rescue. Purchasable from Companies House. Also worth identifying Christopher Bake and Benjamin Monk Johnston as the new controlling parties.

leads_not_followed.what: Onyx's Mira and Mira Pro firmware release history with dates, and whether the GPL matter was ever resolved after 2022
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The single most decision-relevant artefact for this client if he considers a Mira Pro: it would show empirically whether the 25.3in MONITORS get firmware updates or only the tablets do, against Onyx's stated three-year floor. onyxboox.com returned ECONNREFUSED and help.boox.com returned 403. Also worth checking whether the Software Freedom Conservancy or gpl-violations.org ever formally acted.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink Holdings' 2019 strategic investment in Plastic Logic
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Referenced in a June 2019 BusinessWire release that timed out on fetch. Amount, stake and WHICH LEGAL ENTITY received it are unknown — and given that every Plastic Logic entity is now dissolved or in liquidation, this is a documented instance of E Ink writing off an investment in a panel partner. Relevant to judging E Ink's own capital discipline.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink Holdings group headcount
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The only fetchable figure (777) is implausible for a multi-fab manufacturer and MarketScreener's profile returned 403. E Ink's own annual report would settle it. Not decision-critical, but the current number should not be quoted.

leads_not_followed.what: BOE Technology's e-paper investment scale, and LG Display / Tianma large-format e-paper programmes
leads_not_followed.why_promising: An industry SEO page claimed BOE has CNY 46 billion committed to e-paper lines targeting IT and signage, credits LG Display with 3.4 million glass sheets of annual capacity and 24-inch smart-city displays, and Tianma with emerging dual-display work. If anything close to true, BOE is the only credible future SECOND SOURCE to E Ink and would materially change the long-run large-panel supply picture. Note BOE also holds about 25% of VusionGroup, which owns Pervasive Displays — so BOE is already inside this supply chain. Low-quality source; needs primary verification via BOE filings.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether the E Ink / AUO Display Plus term sheet converted into a definitive agreement
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The April 2025 announcement was a TERM SHEET with mass production targeted for Q4 2025. Since this JV is the main structural improvement in large-format module supply, confirming it actually closed and is producing is worth checking in E Ink's or AUO's filings. AUO Display Plus's own site failed DNS resolution.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Melford Technologies' advertised 75in colour e-paper display is E Ink's own 75in Spectra 6 panel
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Melford advertises the largest colour e-paper display of any vendor found. If it is the April-2025 E Ink 75in module in a Melford enclosure, then a UK integrator is already selling the largest colour e-paper display in existence to commercial buyers — potentially the most interesting single lead in this file for a client who wants maximum size in colour.

leads_not_followed.what: Visionect's FY2024 and FY2025 AJPES filings
leads_not_followed.why_promising: My data stops at 2023, which was its FIRST profitable year after two loss years. One year of profit is not a trend, and the February 2026 software-first pivot suggests the hardware business may be under pressure. Slovenian filings are public.

leads_not_followed.what: Chinese corporate registries (Qichacha, Tianyancha) for Guangzhou Onyx Technology, Beijing Dasung Tech, Dalian Good Display and the Bigme parent Xinruizhi
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The only route to registered capital, shareholder lists and paid-in capital for four vendors that disclose nothing voluntarily — including the two (Onyx and Dasung) that actually ship >15in products. Also the route to resolving PocketBook's exact stake percentage in Bigme, which primary reporting calls 'substantial shareholder and co-owner' while secondary databases call it majority or an outright acquisition.

leads_not_followed.why_promising: Fraimic's founder ran Hooke Audio. If the app really was withdrawn and left customers stranded, that is a direct personal precedent for exactly the abandonment the client is screening for, and it would move Fraimic from low to a firm exclusion.

leads_not_followed.why_promising: Material for RMA logistics on $1,300-$4,200 units. I established that Dasung's certified US distributor carries NO 25.3in model and that InkPoster's 'where to buy' page names no retailer at all. Where does a failed panel physically go, and who pays freight? Ask each vendor directly.

leads_not_followed.what: Electronic shelf label majors as demand-side anchors: VusionGroup (Euronext SESL), Pricer AB (Nasdaq Stockholm), Hanshow
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Not art-frame vendors, but they are why E Ink is profitable and expanding — ESL volumes of 500m units in 2025 heading to 600m in 2026 dwarf the art-frame market entirely. Their health is a leading indicator of E Ink's capex appetite and therefore of large-format panel availability. VusionGroup is partly covered above; Hanshow's own about page returned 404 and Pricer was not reached.

leads_not_followed.what: Sun Vision Display 32in reflective LCD monitor
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The only other >15in reflective-display monitor found (32in colour RLCD, FHD at 60Hz, ambient-light-only, announced 2022-02-05). It is RLCD not electrophoretic e-paper, so a different technology and visual result — but it is the only non-E-Ink reflective large display in the field. No entity, funding, headcount, or evidence it ever shipped.

leads_not_followed.what: Named-but-not-found vendors: Kunkun, Sibrena, 'Ink&Art', 'Artframe', 'Lumina'
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Recorded so they are not re-researched. Kunkun returned only an Indonesian architectural-visualisation studio, an Android app developer and an app launcher — no e-paper frame company. Sibrena returned ZERO results. The others surfaced no matching e-paper frame vendors. These are likely bad leads or mis-transcriptions. Note also that 'Palma' is the Boox Palma, a 6in pocket e-reader, not a frame.

leads_not_followed.lead: SwitchBot AI Art Frame undocumented local HTTP endpoints on port 8080. A secondary source states that the pragmatic path for Home Assistant users is 'local network polling via undocumented HTTP endpoints (port 8080), which may break with firmware updates'. I could not confirm this from any primary source, forum thread, or repo.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If real, it would convert the single strongest-staying-power vendor in the category from 'closed / cloud-required' to 'partly-open', and would make the 31.5" SwitchBot the best combined bet in the survey. This is the highest-value open question remaining. Verify by putting a unit on a LAN and port-scanning it, or by searching the Home Assistant community forum and the switchbot subreddit for 'port 8080'.

leads_not_followed.lead: Fraimic's actual local REST API surface. The vendor advertises a REST API and a local-only mode and exposes https://fraimic.local, but publishes no endpoint reference; the official user manual documents only the cloud path. Kickstarter returns 403 to this tool so I could not read the campaign FAQ where the API may be described.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Fraimic Large Canvas is the leading candidate on hardware and price, and its entire abandonment-risk mitigation rests on the local API being real and complete. 'Marketing claims a local API' and 'a documented local API exists' are very different purchases. Verify by browsing http://fraimic.local on a unit and enumerating routes, or by asking Fraimic support directly for the API reference.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the BLOOMIN8 mobile app / initial provisioning requires an arpobot account or cloud round-trip, even though steady-state control is local. support.bloomin8.com returns 403 to this tool and I could not read the Home Assistant support article or the account/privacy documentation.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A cloud-mandatory first-boot would mean the device bricks on activation if arpobot disappears before you set it up, undermining the otherwise excellent survives-the-vendor argument. It would also affect whether a second unit could be commissioned years later.

leads_not_followed.lead: Resolution and PPI of the SwitchBot AI Art Frame 31.5". No page I could read states it. The Fraimic and InkPoster 31.5" units are both 2560x1440 at 94 ppi, strongly suggesting a common E Ink 31.5" Spectra 6 module, but I did not verify SwitchBot uses it.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If SwitchBot's 31.5" is the same 2560x1440 panel, then at $1,299.99 shipping today from a publicly traded vendor it is directly price-comparable to Fraimic's $1,299 and undercuts InkPoster's $1,699 for identical image quality, and the decision reduces cleanly to integration openness versus vendor risk.

leads_not_followed.lead: Six additional colour-ePaper frame brands exhibited at E Ink's photo-frame theme wall at COMPUTEX 2026 that I did not investigate: Aelig, Kokonna, SMARTWIZ+ art, SWISH, YeconTech, and Aipusi (alongside Aura, Bloomin8, InkJoy, PocketBook, Reflection Frame and SwitchBot).
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: One of these could be a >15" entrant nobody has covered. The same source notes the exhibited range spans 7.3" to 40.5" but that '10-inch and 13.3-inch [are] the current mainstream specifications', so the prior is that they are all small - which is why I deprioritised them. Worth a single sweep if the shortlist needs widening.

leads_not_followed.lead: InkPoster Tela 40.5" and Duna 40.5" real ship dates. Both have been 'Notify me' on the vendor's own catalogue for seven months since CES 2026, and the Duna's Engadget-reported April 2026 availability has slipped by four months with no public explanation.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are the only >40" colour options in existence. If they ship, they change the top of the market; if the slip continues, the practical ceiling for a colour art wall stays at 31.5". Worth a direct sales enquiry rather than more web research.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether any of the 28.5"/31.5" frames can be driven at native resolution without the vendor's dithering pipeline. Fraimic (proprietary dithering), Aura (proprietary dithering algorithm), and InkJoy (ISFR engine) all promote in-house image processing; BLOOMIN8 alone exposes an /image/dataUpload endpoint accepting pre-dithered raw data.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: For an art archive, colour fidelity on a 6-ink panel is decided almost entirely by the dithering algorithm. The ability to supply your own pre-dithered data - which only BLOOMIN8 documents - means you can tune reproduction per artwork rather than accepting the vendor's generic photo-optimised pipeline. This may matter more to final image quality than the ppi differences between devices.

leads_not_followed.lead: Visionect (Slovenia) 32" Place & Play e-paper display, positioned as digital signage rather than art.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A >15" reflective e-paper device from a company with a long B2B track record and, being a signage product, likely a far more open management/API story than any consumer art frame. It is monochrome and not marketed as art, so it falls outside the literal scope, but as a self-hosted-archive display it may be a better engineering fit than several in-scope consumer frames. I did not research it.

leads_not_followed.lead: Korean-language search was never run. Chinese and Japanese searches each produced a major find that no English query surfaced (Guangzhou OED, Teidec).
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Korea has Samsung, LG and SOLUM all shipping large-format e-paper, so a domestic supplier/integrator tier almost certainly exists and is invisible to English search. This is the single highest-value remaining gap and the main reason my saturation claim should be read as 'saturated in English, Chinese and Japanese' rather than absolutely.

leads_not_followed.lead: epaperia.org's 'Industry Database' and 'ePaper Mall' sections were not enumerated - only the member list on the landing page was. The site claims 260+ member resources; I captured 16.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This one page produced more new names than any other source in the sweep. The remaining ~244 resources are the densest unexplored vein available, and the ePaper Mall in particular would give product-level data rather than just company names.

leads_not_followed.lead: The Alibaba OEM/ODM tier (Shenzhen Caison, Leeka Electronic, Elsun, Shangtuo Semicon, Startek, Minew, Clientop, Zemso, Veto, Refee, Zhejiang Sunparl, Zhuhai Suny) was recorded as a class but not individually verified. Alibaba reports 762 e-paper-with-WiFi suppliers.

Worth one focused pass if price is the binding constraint.

leads_not_followed.lead: Samsung's 32in EMDX retail SKU advertises USB Type-C compatibility, and Nanov's 32in runs Android 10.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are the two most promising undocumented local-push surfaces found. A USB-C port that accepts an image, or an Android controller reachable over ADB, would each bypass the cloud CMS entirely on hardware that is otherwise closed. Neither is documented anywhere I looked; both are testable with a unit in hand.

leads_not_followed.lead: Cayin Technology's claim to connect with 'any e-paper device, regardless of brand, model or size' was not technically verified.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If real, it is a brand-agnostic content layer across otherwise incompatible panels - which would change the buying calculus from 'pick the vendor with the best API' to 'pick the best panel'. The press coverage contained no protocols, no API detail, and no supported-device list, so it may be marketing.

leads_not_followed.lead: paperlesspaper's API docs were only read at the landing-page level. Whether the API terminates locally on the device or requires paperlesspaper's servers was not resolved.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is the decisive question for the single best self-hosting candidate found. Open hardware plus a cloud-dependent API would be materially less useful than it appears. The endpoint reference and Getting Started sections would settle it.

leads_not_followed.lead: Guangzhou OED's own website, pricing, and panel availability to third parties were not investigated.

leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Teidec's microSD standalone mode on a 40.5in A1 colour panel is the only fully offline path to a large colour display found in the entire sweep. If it can be bought outside Japan at a sane price, it is arguably the best answer to the brief's underlying question.

leads_not_followed.lead: Sharp's ePoster A0 (57in) and A1 (40in) models were referenced only via a secondary description of the size ladder, not confirmed on Sharp's own product pages.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: 57in would be the largest non-tiled reflective panel in the survey. The size ladder came from an invidis summary of Sharp's range rather than a Sharp source, so it needs confirmation.

leads_not_followed.lead: Trade-show exhibitor lists were sampled (Touch Taiwan, ISE, InfoComm, EuroShop) but never enumerated systematically - I read coverage of the shows rather than the raw exhibitor directories.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: The one exhibitor list I did touch produced Hanjentek and M2COMM, neither of which any product search found. Walking the actual ISE and InfoComm e-paper exhibitor directories would likely produce a similar yield of integrator-tier names.

leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: It is the only genuinely unrecorded consumer art-frame brand found, but sizes, price and whether it exceeds 13in are all unknown, so it cannot be placed in or out of scope.

leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are segment-adjacent rather than art-relevant - Ynvisible's displays are segmented/low-information rather than pixel-addressable - but they represent the alternative-technology branch that could eventually produce a cheaper large reflective panel.

leads_not_followed.lead: Touch Taiwan 電子紙應用 exhibitor list at touchtaiwan.com/Display/en/visitorExhibitor.asp?Area=1920 returned HTTP 403.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: E Ink assembled 101 supply-chain partners into an ePaper Pavilion. This is the single largest directly enumerable list of e-paper companies in existence and I could not open it. It would likely double the vendor count on its own.

leads_not_followed.lead: epaperia.com industry database at /Search.html - the alliance's 260+ member directory.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: I fetched the landing page and the council-member page, which together named about 25 companies. The searchable database behind /Search.html holds the other ~235. It is the definitive map of the Chinese long tail.

leads_not_followed.lead: Alibaba and 1688 product pages are unfetchable (empty bodies) and Zhihu returns 403.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Roughly 15 marketplace ODMs in this report rest on an AI aggregator's secondhand reading of Alibaba listings rather than the listings themselves. Price and MOQ figures for that tier should be re-verified by a human with a browser before anyone acts on them.

leads_not_followed.lead: Metoree's Japanese ranking of 26+ 電子ペーパー manufacturers returned 403.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Japan produced three genuinely new integrators (CREA, TEIDEC, StellarLink) from a single search. A full Japanese vendor list would likely yield several more, and Japanese vendors are unusually forthcoming about local connectivity (RJ-45, HDMI, USB).

leads_not_followed.lead: Guangdong Mingjinkang's 25.3in colour poster at USD 390-430 MOQ 1, reportedly RK3566-based.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If real, it is a third of the price of any comparable unit and an Android SoC would likely permit ADB-based local pushing. This is the single highest-value item to verify with a direct quote.

leads_not_followed.lead: CREA's HDMI input on its 42in and 32in monochrome e-paper signage.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: HDMI on an EPD is nearly unheard of and would let an ordinary computer drive a 42in e-paper panel with no vendor software at all. Worth confirming directly with CREA, including whether the colour models have it.

leads_not_followed.lead: Good Display's ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U mainboard in the 31.5in DMPH315E6x, plus downloadable XTacepSetup and Smart EPD APP.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: An ESP32-S3 is fully documented and reflashable. This is the most plausible route to a genuinely open local-push 31.5in colour display. Someone should dump the firmware and see whether the WiFi update path is a plain HTTP endpoint.

leads_not_followed.lead: Agile Conversion Engine (ACE) middleware and its new Navori Labs CMS bridge.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: First middleware to make e-paper drivable from a mainstream CMS. Agile's country and corporate identity were not stated in E Ink's release and could not be established without guessing.

leads_not_followed.lead: AUO Display Plus / E Ink joint venture output and which brands it is building for.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: StellarLink's aecoPost is one confirmed badge. Identifying the rest would reveal how much of the 31.5in market is a single Taoyuan production line under different logos - important for judging whether vendor diversity is real or cosmetic.

leads_not_followed.lead: Laibao Hi-Tech's MED (micro-cavity display) programme.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A ~USD 1.2bn bet on a non-E-Ink reflective technology. Currently zero revenue and stalled, but it is the only credible path to breaking the film monopoly at scale. Worth a status check annually.

leads_not_followed.lead: 13.3in consumer art frames sold single-unit in the West: Huessen EPF1301 (B&H, Petra), Aluratek, InkPoster, eco4lifehome.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are the only large colour e-paper products confirmed purchasable by an individual through normal retail with app/cloud sync. Their integration openness was never examined in this sweep because the brief pointed at Asian ODMs.

leads_not_followed.lead: Sharp EP-C251 (25.3in) and EP-421 (42in) individual spec pages.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Only the 13.3in EP-C131 page was fetched. The 25.3in colour model in particular may have better connectivity than the 13.3in, which lacks WiFi and LAN entirely.

leads_not_followed.lead: Shenzhen Gode Xinc's 超稳态液晶显示技术 (ultra-stable LCD).
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A reflective display route that is neither electrophoretic nor ChLCD, surfaced only in the alliance council list. Unexamined.

leads_not_followed.lead: Chinese government procurement records (中标公告) for e-paper bus-stop and signage deployments.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Tender awards name the actual winning integrators with prices, which is far harder evidence than marketplace listings. A Yangzhou e-paper bus-stop pilot surfaced in search but was not pursued.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the 42in class is E Ink's ED420TT1 panel in every case.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Sharp, CREA, DKE, Holitech, Good Display and ATZ all offer a 42in monochrome. If they are all the same panel, the apparent vendor diversity at 42in is one panel with six badges.

leads_not_followed.lead: The full ePaper Industry Alliance member database at epaperia.org/Search.html and the per-member pages at /Members/[ID].html. EPIA claims 150-260+ members; roughly 50 were visible to me without registration.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is the single highest-leverage remaining action and the structural fix for the sampling gap the brief describes. A registered account would enumerate the whole industry in one pass instead of vendor-by-vendor searching. Their 'ePaper Mall' also publishes actual prices, which almost no vendor does.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether Advantech's DeviceOn/ePaper exposes a scriptable REST API for pushing an image to a specific display. Their ESS-WIKI documentation host (ess-wiki.advantech.com.tw) did not resolve for me.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Advantech is the best overall candidate found - 28.6 inch Spectra 6 at 3060x2160, USB and Ethernet, and a management server that installs on your own Ubuntu box. The only missing fact is whether the archive could script image pushes rather than clicking through a web UI. That one answer would likely settle the whole search.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the LG 32-inch e-paper display accepts USB media or local-network content directly through webOS, without SuperSign.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A tier-1 manufacturer, 32 inch, QHD, colour, battery-powered. LG's webOS signage line has historically supported USB playback. If that carries over, this becomes a mainstream, well-supported, no-cloud option - the most durable of any candidate here.

leads_not_followed.lead: AUO Display Plus's aecoPost integration model. Their product page 404'd; AUO Display Plus exists specifically to sell finished units to integrators and end customers.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: 31.5 inch Spectra 6 at 2560x1440 is arguably the best artwork panel found, from a tier-1 manufacturer with an integrator-friendly sales posture. Only the content-delivery mechanism is unknown.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether TintTech or Artec Design plan a colour (Spectra 6) panel, or would build one on commission.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: They already have the hard part - a self-hosted Debian CMS with a REST API, a perpetual licence and no cloud. Their only disqualifier is that every panel they sell is greyscale. A colour variant would make them the outright best fit for this use case.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the Agile ACE 'open integration standard' has, or will have, a self-hostable reference implementation or published interface specification.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: ACE is the only attempt in this industry to standardise the CMS-to-e-paper interface. Today it is cloud-only, which blocks self-hosting. If it opens up it would unlock the largest panels in the segment (75 inch) and many vendors at once.

leads_not_followed.lead: Sharp's EP-C251 full datasheet - specifically whether the PC connection is a scriptable interface or a manual desktop utility. Sharp's global and NEC-branded e-paper pages both 404'd or redirected away.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: USB-C thumbdrive loading on a 25.3 inch colour panel from a tier-1 manufacturer is the single most promising local-push signal found. Whether it can be automated determines if it suits a self-hosted archive app or only manual curation.

leads_not_followed.lead: Six OEM names (Fortune Achieve, Shenzhen Huayi, Shenzhen Chance Technology, Shenzhen Startek, Dongguan VETO, Guangzhou Zemso) that appeared only in AI-generated aggregator summaries on accio.com, which I deliberately did not fetch.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Probably real Alibaba-tier OEMs at 25.3 and 31.5 inch, but the only source was a synthesised aggregator page - exactly the kind of source that produces fabricated specifications. Listed for completeness; would need first-party verification before being treated as real.

leads_not_followed.lead: HKC's claim of e-paper displays 'over 50 inches'.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If true this would be the second-largest single e-paper panel in existence after the 75 inch units. HKC published no model names or specifications to support it, so it stays unverified.

leads_not_followed.lead: Transit integrators Journeo, Aesys and Trueform, and the transit-authority procurement channel generally.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Probably a dead end for this use case - they sell managed transit infrastructure to public authorities, not displays to individuals - but they are large-format e-paper buyers and their supplier lists would name panel vendors.

leads_not_followed.lead: Reddit entirely (r/eink, r/einkdisplays, r/homeassistant, r/functionalprint). Every fetch attempt - www.reddit.com/r/eink/search.json and old.reddit.com/r/eink/search - was refused outright by the fetch tool, and site:reddit.com searches returned zero Reddit results.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This was a named primary surface in the brief and it is completely unsampled. Reddit is where owners post the unflattering facts (ghosting, refresh artefacts, app quality, whether cloud is really optional) and where small makers get named. Treat this as an unexplored surface, not a saturated one - anything found there would be additive to this report.

leads_not_followed.lead: Kickstarter, Crowd Supply, Etsy and Amazon product pages all returned HTTP 403/500. LumiCap, InkJoy, Memoir/Zyvoralabs, LINKUADRO and Inkanva could not be read first-party.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: LumiCap and LINKUADRO have no diagonal or price recorded anywhere fetchable, so they are in this report as names only. A human with a browser can resolve all five in about ten minutes.

leads_not_followed.lead: Inkanva (inkanva.com) - pre-launch, claims Spectra 6 HD, perovskite indoor-light solar harvesting for 'infinite battery', and an OpenAPI for AI-agent automation. No size, resolution or price disclosed.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If the OpenAPI claim is real it would join Fraimic/BLOOMIN8/TintTech in the small set of genuinely programmable frames, and indoor-light solar would remove the recharge problem entirely at large sizes. Currently pure marketing - not one verifiable spec. Worth a revisit when the Kickstarter goes live.

leads_not_followed.lead: Easyblock (Yiboluoke) 'MoQu' art frame, crowdfunded in China, full-colour E6 with low-power WiFi module and an app supporting scheduled refresh, carousels and remote push.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Diagonal is not stated on the page I fetched, so I could not confirm it clears 13". The Chinese domestic market appears to have its own crowdfunded frames with no Western coverage at all - einkcn.com is the aggregator to mine if that market matters.

leads_not_followed.lead: PicPak by AutoHeart - E Ink frame with a claimed 400-day battery, covered by iGeneration (FR) in Jan 2026.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Almost certainly well under 13" so out of scope, but it is another entrant absent from every English roundup, reinforcing that non-English search is where the long tail lives.

leads_not_followed.lead: The 25.3" and 31.5" Spectra 6 panels are on sale retail from E Ink at $1,400 with no known MCU-class controller and no community build log.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is the single biggest open question for DIY at large sizes. MpicoSys TCM2/TCM3 cover 28"/31.2"/42" but only in monochrome as far as their published list goes. Somebody needs to answer 'what actually drives a 25.3" Spectra 6' - a direct enquiry to MpicoSys or E Ink would settle it.

leads_not_followed.lead: E Ink shopkits 'Partner's Solutions' category (91 items total in the shop) - I enumerated the panels and the driving-board codenames but did not open the partner listings individually.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: The two partner entries I did open (Visionect, Digital View) were both new names with large-format products and real APIs. The remaining partner listings are a concentrated, high-yield source that I only sampled.

leads_not_followed.lead: The 'is it the same frame in different wood' question. Aluratek, eco4life, Huessen, YIAIFRAME and the generic Amazon listings all quote 13.3" / 1600x1200 / Spectra 6 / ~5000 mAh / ~6-18 months / app-over-WiFi.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If these are all SeekInk or AVLink reference designs, then brand choice at 13.3" is a choice of enclosure, warranty and app - not of hardware. Confirming this would collapse a large part of the apparent variety in this market and is answerable by comparing FCC IDs.

leads_not_followed.lead: orientdisplay.com 'E-ink Digital Art Frame Introduction' returned HTTP 403.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Orient Display is another display supplier that appears to be entering the art-frame space; unread.

leads_not_followed.lead: The ~208 EPIA members visible only behind registration. Registration is free-form ([Register] then [Login]) and would unlock /SearchQuery with PSize paging plus the 72-value advanced-search filter set, including the 'Applcations of large size ePaper' tag that would isolate exactly the target population in one query.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is now the single highest-value unexplored source in the entire survey, and unlike the rest of the web it is a structured, filterable database with a large-size-ePaper facet built in. Four times more members sit behind the login than in front of it. I did not register because creating an account is an action requiring the owner's consent, not a research technique. Worth an explicit decision.

leads_not_followed.lead: ADLAB's actual image-load mechanism for WYED312L / WYED280L / WYED133C. The spec sheets prove Linux, USB-A host, RJ45 and removable micro-SD system storage, but the update path is entirely undocumented publicly.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are the best-shaped candidates found for an offline archive and the only >=13in units with confirmed Ethernet plus USB host plus removable storage. Whether they take a file over the LAN or need a vendor tool is the whole decision. One email to the Taipei office (+886-2-8791-8368) resolves it. Their 28in Android sibling has an explicit SD slot, so a sideloadable variant of the 31.2in may already exist.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the AUO Display Plus AecoPost mobile app accepts arbitrary full-resolution user images, and whether the advertised 'API integration with existing CMS' is available without a commercial IMPRESS contract.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: AecoPost 31.5in Mobile is the best large colour candidate found, and the existence of a separate Cloud SKU strongly implies the Mobile SKU works without any vendor service. If the app takes arbitrary JPEGs over Bluetooth, this is a cloud-free 31.5in Spectra 6 art display available today.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the Modos Paper Dev Kit's panel-agnostic FPGA controller can actually drive a 25.3in or 31.5in E Ink panel sourced separately from DKE or E Ink.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is the only route found to a LARGE display with a fully open, vendor-independent image path. The dev kit is explicitly described as supporting a range of E Ink panels and the Caster gateware is open source. If it scales past 13.3in it dominates every other option on the openness axis. Requires reading the Caster repository and the panel timing requirements.

leads_not_followed.lead: TPV's 31.2in and 42in black-and-white ePaper signage, reported in secondary coverage but never confirmed against a TPV or E Ink primary page.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: 42in would be the largest single-panel e-paper signage anywhere in this survey. TPV is also the manufacturing parent behind the already-known Philips/PPDS brand, so this may be the industrial origin of a product the survey already holds under another name -- a possible duplicate worth resolving.

leads_not_followed.lead: Suzhou Etag's 'ePaper industrial flat panel' product, and Ink Cubic's corporate identity.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Etag's industrial flat panel is the one EPIA product description suggesting a large-format unit whose size was never published. Ink Cubic is an E Ink-named module manufacturer with effectively zero public footprint -- both need Chinese-language corporate-registry or Made-in-China searches rather than general web search.

leads_not_followed.lead: The named sellers behind the two EPIA ePaper Mall listings (13.3in Spectra 6 at 499-599 and 31.5in Spectra 6 at 1199-1299). The mall shows products without attributing vendors.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are the lowest prices seen for finished Spectra 6 units at these sizes, materially below Western consumer art-frame pricing for the same panel. Identifying the seller (each /Mall/<n>.html detail page may name it) could find a direct source. I fetched only the mall index, not the nine individual listing pages.

leads_not_followed.lead: Korean marketplace indexes -- Naver Smart Store, Danawa, Coupang, 11st -- which this search tool does not surface directly.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Low expected value but it is the honest residual gap in the Korean saturation claim. Any seller found there would be reselling Samsung/LG/imported units rather than manufacturing, so it would change the vendor list little. Would require driving a browser against Naver directly.

leads_not_followed.lead: eleparts.co.kr's E-PAPER catalogue, which returned an empty body when fetched.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Korean component distributor; would establish which e-paper modules are stocked domestically in Korea and at what KRW prices. Minor, but it is the one Korean source that failed for technical rather than substantive reasons.

leads_not_followed.lead: Nooka Art's 'Light Dynamic Wave' e-paper installation in a ribbon window at the Taipei Dome
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A second architectural-scale ART installation on e-paper, in Asia, by a studio nobody in this survey has looked at. Surfaced only in a search summary; I never fetched a page about it, so it is unverified. Worth one fetch of Nooka Art's own site.

leads_not_followed.lead: 3Form's 'Viva' architectural material co-developed with E Ink
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: An architectural-materials company embedding e-paper into panels. If e-paper is being sold as an interior surface rather than a screen, that is a different procurement channel with different sizes.

leads_not_followed.lead: Review Display Systems' actual e-paper product catalogue
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Their claim of 32in e-paper modules with bespoke firmware and APIs is the single most interesting integrator claim found. Their own product URL 404'd. A direct enquiry would settle whether a UK integrator will build a custom colour e-paper display with a local API.

leads_not_followed.lead: CREA's 42in EPS pricing and whether they will export outside Japan
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: CREA is the only vendor found with HDMI input plus SD card plus FTP on a 42in e-paper panel. Everything about the architecture fits; the unknowns are price, export, and whether the s-color line will ever reach 42in.

leads_not_followed.lead: Guangzhou OED's 31.2in colour e-paper at 18fps entering mass production
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A non-E-Ink colour electrophoretic panel at 30in+ would be the first real price competition in the category. Known vendor, but the mass-production claim from March 2025 was never followed up to see if it shipped.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether Philips Tableaux's Android SoC will run a sideloaded app
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If it will, a 32in Spectra 6 colour panel becomes drivable from a self-hosted server with no PPDS cloud - which would change the answer for this project. The Institut Pasteur deployment proves third-party software (Telelogos) can drive it.

leads_not_followed.lead: E Ink Prism / Prism 3 availability to non-automotive, non-architectural buyers
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Prism is the only E Ink product line with a documented history of being used for actual commissioned artwork (DAZZLE, BMW NOSTOKANA). It is a segmented film, not an image display, so it cannot show a painting - but it is worth knowing whether E Ink still sells it at all.

leads_not_followed.lead: Heureka Science Centre (Helsinki) and the National Museum in Krakow as TintTech references
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Two more museum deployments of the PoE + self-hosted-CMS architecture. They appeared in search summaries of TintTech material but not on the references page I fetched.

unverified_facts.claim: SwitchBot AI Art Frame can be controlled locally over HTTP on port 8080 without the SwitchBot cloud.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Asserted by a single secondary aggregator page that surfaced in search results. No primary source, no repo, no forum thread, and no vendor documentation corroborates it. I did not read the page it came from and am not citing it. Treat as rumour until tested on hardware.

unverified_facts.claim: The SwitchBot AI Art Frame 31.5" uses a 2560x1440 panel at ~94 ppi.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Inferred from the fact that both other 31.5" Spectra 6 art frames (Fraimic Large Canvas and InkPoster Affresco 31.5") independently specify 2560x1440 at 94 DPI, implying a single E Ink module. No SwitchBot page I could read states any resolution for the 31.5" model.

unverified_facts.claim: Anthony Mattana (Fraimic CEO) sold a previous company to Logitech.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Stated in a podcast show-notes page, which did not name the company. His documented prior venture is Hooke Audio. I found no filing, press release, or Logitech announcement confirming an acquisition, and no source connecting him to the 2014 Hush smart-earplug campaign despite the surface similarity.

unverified_facts.claim: IONNYK Linn and Maxine display diagonals are 31.2" and 40.2" respectively.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Computed by me from the display AREAS published on ionnyk.com (69 x 39 cm and 82 x 61 cm). IONNYK publishes frame dimensions and display areas but never a diagonal or a resolution, and I could not reach any retailer spec sheet (luxuryformen returns 403). Published secondary figures for these frames are unreliable - one roundup reports IONNYK sizes by taking the frame dimensions as the screen.

unverified_facts.claim: Aura Frames has raised USD 46.9M lifetime over 8 rounds and has 125 employees; and separately, that its revenue is USD 3.7M ARR.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Both come from data-aggregator pages (Tracxn, GetLatka) that appeared in search results and that I did not fetch. The $3.7M revenue figure is flatly inconsistent with ~1M frames sold at $149-$499 and is very likely wrong. The verified figure is ~USD 39M raised as of the 2022 TechCrunch round.

unverified_facts.claim: MelonFrame's largest model is 13.3" and Memoir's three sizes are all under 15".
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Neither vendor publishes a screen size anywhere I could read, including MelonFrame's own support pages. Kickstarter returns 403 to this tool. The 13.3 diagonals recorded for both are upper-bound inferences from price points ($99 and $149 entry) and from the fact that the E Ink consumer frame market's stated mainstream sizes are 10" and 13.3". They are not measurements.

unverified_facts.claim: InkJoy Frame will be offered in a size larger than 13.3".
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The vendor says only that 'multiple frame sizes will be available' and publishes no list. I could not fetch the Kickstarter campaign (403) or the one review carrying specs (content truncated). The 13.3 recorded is an assumption, not a fact.

unverified_facts.claim: Fraimic Large Canvas units are actually in customers' hands.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Three sources disagree as of early August 2026: Forbes (2026-07-21) says 'shipping now'; fraimic.com's product page says 'Ships Early August'; the shop collection shows both SKUs 'Sold out'; and BackerGuardian (2026-07-27) found no public confirmation of any backer delivery against a promised May 2026 date. The only reviewed unit anywhere was a preproduction 13.3". No independent confirmation of a delivered 31.5" exists.

unverified_facts.claim: The BLOOMIN8 local REST API is genuinely unauthenticated on the LAN.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The published openapi.yaml declares no security scheme and the HA component README documents no authentication, which together strongly imply an open endpoint - but absence of a declaration in a spec is not proof of absence in firmware, and the Schedule Pull configuration does involve a token for the upstream direction. Confirm on hardware before designing around it, and note that an unauthenticated endpoint is itself a LAN security consideration for the installation.

unverified_facts.claim: PocketBook International SA is the direct legal owner of the IONNYK entity (as opposed to an affiliate or holding company being the acquirer).
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The acquisition is well documented in PocketBook's own announcement and in trade press, but no source I read named the acquiring legal entity or disclosed the transaction structure or price. The InkPoster-to-PocketBook relationship IS directly verified (inkposter.com's about page names Pocketbook International SA).

unverified_facts.claim: paperlesspaper's openpaper L can be driven entirely from a local server with no dependency on paperlesspaper's cloud.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The product page and the API docs landing page both confirm an open-source device and a documented API, but neither states where the API terminates. I did not read the endpoint reference. Plausible given the open-hardware stance, but not established.

unverified_facts.claim: Glory Star's 'Star Control' is a local/LAN image-push tool rather than a cloud service.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The e-paper landing page names Star Control and links a tutorial, but does not say whether it is desktop software, a LAN service or a cloud platform. The detailed product page was truncated on fetch.

unverified_facts.claim: Nanov's 32in Android 10 controller exposes ADB, allowing direct image push.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Android 10 is confirmed as the built-in system by product coverage, but ADB availability is my inference from the platform, not a documented vendor capability. Commercial signage builds frequently disable ADB.

unverified_facts.claim: Cayin's e-paper integration genuinely works with any e-paper device regardless of brand.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: This is the vendor's own claim as reported in trade press. No protocols, no API surface and no supported-device list were published, and I found no independent verification.

unverified_facts.claim: Sharp's ePoster line spans A3 20in, A2 28in, A1 40in and A0 57in.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: This size ladder came from an invidis article describing Sharp's range in the context of the Tisensi partnership, not from Sharp's own product documentation. The separately confirmed Sharp products are the 42in monochrome, 25.3in and 13.3in.

unverified_facts.claim: Guangzhou OED's 31.2in panel is available for purchase by third parties.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Coverage says OED 'is making and shipping' 31.2in colour displays, but does not say to whom or in what form (bare panel, module, or only through the Geniatech partnership). I did not fetch OED's own site.

unverified_facts.claim: Samsung's 32in EMDX USB Type-C port accepts image content for display.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The Amazon retail listing advertises 'USB Type-C Compatibility' but does not say what that means functionally - it may be power-only, or for firmware/service. No documentation found either way.

unverified_facts.claim: Teidec's e-paper signage is purchasable outside Japan.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The product page is Japanese-language with no international ordering path, no pricing and no distributor list. Japan-only distribution is likely but not confirmed.

unverified_facts.claim: Visionect has substantially exited hardware in favour of software.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: Based on an invidis headline and summary from February 2026 ('E-Paper Pioneer Shifts Focus to Software'). I did not fetch the article body, so the extent of the shift - and whether Place & Play hardware remains orderable - is unestablished. This matters because Visionect has been the default self-hostable 32in option.

unverified_facts.claim: The 'E Ink D-Poster' (32in Spectra 6, 3060x2160, 130 PPI, ~17s per image transition, Bluetooth 5.2, 4kg) is a purchasable product rather than a reference design.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: These specifications came from a Good e-Reader summary returned in search results. The custom CMS mentioned suggests a reference/OEM design rather than a retail SKU, and it does not appear in the E Ink shopkit catalogue I fetched.

unverified_facts.claim: The various 31.5in posters sold by StellarLink, AUO Display Plus, TCL CSOT, Hanjentek, Glory Star, Praevar and SwitchBot are substantially the same underlying AUO/E Ink hardware.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The StellarLink aecoPost is explicitly confirmed as AUO Display Plus manufactured, and AUO has a confirmed large-format JV with E Ink. Extending that to the other 31.5in products is a reasonable inference from the convergent 2560x1440 Spectra 6 spec, but it is an inference, not a documented fact.

delivery_record.headline_answer: YES. The premise that no >15-inch e-paper frame has ever reached a real owner is FALSE, and it is false twice over. (1) Retail: PocketBook's InkPoster Tela 28.5in ($2,399) and Affresco 31.5in ($1,699) have been on general sale in the US since roughly Nov-Dec 2025, are 'Add to cart' in stock today, and an independent reviewer (Fstoppers, 21 Dec 2025) physically received and photographed one. (2) Crowdfunded: Fraimic's Large Canvas (31.5in Spectra 6) began shipping to Kickstarter backers in the last week of July 2026, and named backers posted receipt confirmations on the campaign's public comment wall on 4-5 Aug 2026 ('the Large frame came today', 'I am backer 1102 and I just received 1 large (31 inch) screen... works great'). So 'open but risky' does NOT collapse into 'does not exist'. What IS true is that the specific vendors the survey flagged as most open are the ones still not delivering at size: BLOOMIN8's 28.5in is ~10 months past its promised October 2025 date with zero backers reporting a unit, and InkJoy's 25.3in/28.5in are ~3 months late with production only targeted for mid-August 2026. Both those vendors HAVE delivered their small (7.3in-13.3in) SKUs, so the pattern is not 'vendor cannot ship', it is 'the large panel is the part that slips'. And the true horror story in this category is Galari (Kyoto): $339,557 from 737 backers in March 2025, promised September 2025, and as of August 2026 still has no supplier for the panel and is redesigning its PCB.

historical_precedents.what_happened: VERIFIED IN SUBSTANCE, WRONG IN ONE DETAIL. The bricking story is real and corroborated by two independent sources. Memento sold a ~35-inch, 3:2, 4K digital art frame for approaching $900, funded via Kickstarter around 2016. The company went out of business in late 2018 / 2018-19. The frame was 100% cloud-dependent: 'The only way to get photos onto the frame is through the app via the cloud servers', and even the USB port required an active server connection, so when the servers went dark owners could not load images and could not even complete initial setup. Frames became, in the sources' words, 'an expensive paperweight'. A small community keeps a minority of units alive. THE CORRECTION: Memento was NOT an e-paper frame - it was a high-resolution emissive panel. Do not cite it as an e-paper precedent; cite it as the canonical cloud-dependency precedent, which is how the independent e-ink frame reviewer actually uses it.

sources.what_it_supports: Out of business late 2018; ~$900; 35in 4K 3:2; cloud-only image path including a USB port that needed the server; 'expensive paperweight'

Independent corroboration from an e-ink frame reviewer: 'Memento is a good example of what can go wrong: once its servers were shut down, the owners were left with expensive, essentially useless hardware' - and it is used explicitly as the reason to prefer cloud-free frames

historical_precedents.product: Electric Objects EO1 / EO2 digital art frame
historical_precedents.what_happened: A second, independent instance of the same failure mode, and the closest analogue to this buyer's use case (an internet-connected fine-art display). Electric Objects raised on Kickstarter in 2014, shipped EO1 and EO2, was acquired by GIPHY in 2017, and the hardware team was wound down. Years later owners report the EO2 can no longer be reconnected to Wi-Fi because the configuration app is gone from the App Store, so a device that is physically fine is unrecoverable. CAVEAT ON MY SOURCING: the owner report I fetched (comedian Adam Conover's Mastodon post) returned only the opening fragment 'My beloved Electric Objects EO2 digital art frame...' - I could not retrieve the full text or its date from that page, and the supporting detail about the app removal came from search-result summaries I did not independently open. Treat the specifics as medium-confidence; treat the pattern (art-frame company acquired, service and app abandoned, hardware stranded) as well-established.

sources.what_it_supports: An owner publicly complaining about an EO2 digital art frame; I could only extract the opening fragment of the post, so this supports 'an owner posted about it', not the full detail

historical_precedents.what_happened: The best-documented in-category crowdfunding failure to date, and it is CURRENT, not historical. Funded 26 March 2025 at 1,700% of goal ($339,557 / 737 backers / Project We Love badge), promised September 2025. Seventeen months after funding and eleven months past the promise, there is still no panel supplier and the PCB is being redesigned; the demonstrated prototype turns out to have been a Raspberry Pi driving off-the-shelf Waveshare modules. Refunds are being refused on the grounds that the money is committed. Note that the vendor is still communicating monthly - so 'vendor still posts updates' is NOT a safety signal.
